newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea's Jan-Mar imports of corn down, soybean up.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea's Jan-Mar imports of corn down, soybean up.

text.p: South Korea's corn imports fell by 16.3 percent to 1,864,740 tonnes in the first three months of 1997 from 2,227,755 tonnes a year ago, an official with the Korea International Trade Association (KITA) said on Friday.
South Korea's imports from the United States fell by 16.8 percent to 1,853,155 tonnes for the first quarter from 2,227,755 tonnes a year earlier, the official said.

However, the country's soybean imports rose by 8.2 percent to 340,897 tonnes for the period from 315,125 tonnes a year ago and wheat imports rose by 11.8 percent to 730,181 tonnes for the same period from 653,121 tonnes a year earlier, he said.
Soybean imports from the United States rose to 338,862 tonnes for the first quarter from 314,127 tonnes a year ago, he said.

In a reference to wheat imports, he said the United States supplied 403,200 tonnes in the first three months, compared to 345,062 tonnes a year ago. Wheat imports from Canada for the period rose to 186,141 tonnes from 125,435 tonnes a year earlier and from Australia also rose 134,640 tonnes from 118,624 tonnes.
Soymeal imports for the period fell to 159,521 tonnes from 296,624 tonnes a year ago, he said. Imports from Brazil fell to 70,779 tonnes from 150,225 tonnes a year earlier.

Soymeal imports from India totalled 74,226 tonnes, compared with 143,198 tonnes for the same period last year, while imports from Argentina rose to 14,500 tonnes from 1,075 tonnes a year ago. -- Seoul Newsroom (822) 727 5651
